title: 354. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Chord Length and Distance from Center
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Perpendicular from Center to a Chord
questions.learningObjective: Identify the effect of a perpendicular from the center to a chord.
questions.question: In a circle, a perpendicular segment is drawn from the center to a chord. What does this segment do to the chord?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes the chord twice as long.

questions.explanation: A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord. This means it divides the chord into two equal segments.
questions.hint: Recall the standard theorem relating the center, a chord, and a perpendicular to the chord.

questions.concept: Chord Length from Radius and Distance
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the length of a chord given the radius and the distance from the center.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(5\text{ cm}\). A chord is \(3\text{ cm}\) from the center. What is the length of the chord?
questions.explanation:
The radius, half the chord, and the distance from the center form a right triangle. Half the chord is
\[
\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=\sqrt{25-9}=\sqrt{16}=4\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, the full chord is \(2\times4=8\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use the right triangle formed by the radius, half the chord, and the distance from the center.

questions.concept: Distance from Center from Chord Length
questions.learningObjective: Find the distance from the center given the chord length and radius.
questions.question: A chord of length \(24\text{ cm}\) is in a circle of radius \(13\text{ cm}\). What is the distance from the center to the chord?
questions.explanation:
Half the chord is \(24\div2=12\text{ cm}\). The distance \(d\) from the center satisfies
\[
d=\sqrt{13^2-12^2}=\sqrt{169-144}=\sqrt{25}=5\text{ cm}.
\]
So the distance is \(5\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use half the chord and the radius as the legs and hypotenuse of a right triangle.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the property of equal chords in a circle.
questions.question: In the same circle, what is true about two equal chords?

options.label: A
options.text: They are equidistant from the center.

options.label: B
options.text: They must intersect at the center.

questions.explanation: In a circle, equal chords are equidistant from the center. This means the perpendicular distances from the center to the two chords are equal. Equal chords do not necessarily pass through the center.
questions.hint: Recall the theorem connecting equal chord lengths with equal distances from the center.

questions.concept: Chord Length and Distance from Center
questions.learningObjective: Compare the distances from the center for chords of different lengths.
questions.question: In the same circle, chord \(AB\) is \(16\text{ cm}\) and chord \(CD\) is \(12\text{ cm}\). Which chord is farther from the center?
questions.explanation: In the same circle, a longer chord is closer to the center, and a shorter chord is farther from the center. Since \(12<16\), chord \(CD\) is shorter and therefore farther from the center.
questions.hint: Compare the chord lengths and recall which chord is farther from the center.

questions.concept: Distance from Center from Chord Length
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the distance from the center given the chord length and radius.
questions.question: A chord of length \(12\text{ cm}\) is in a circle of radius \(10\text{ cm}\). What is the distance from the center to the chord?
questions.explanation:
Half the chord is \(12\div2=6\text{ cm}\). The distance \(d\) is
\[
d=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=\sqrt{100-36}=\sqrt{64}=8\text{ cm}.
\]
So the distance is \(8\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: First find half the chord, then use the Pythagorean theorem.

questions.concept: Chord Length from Radius and Distance
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the length of a chord given the radius and the distance from the center.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(10\text{ cm}\). A chord is \(6\text{ cm}\) from the center. What is the length of the chord?
questions.explanation:
Half the chord is
\[
\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=\sqrt{100-36}=\sqrt{64}=8\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, the full chord is \(2\times8=16\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use half the chord, the radius, and the distance from the center in a right triangle.

questions.concept: Distance from Center from Chord Length
questions.learningObjective: Find the distance from the center given the chord length and radius.
questions.question: A chord of length \(8\text{ cm}\) is in a circle of radius \(5\text{ cm}\). What is the distance from the center to the chord?
questions.explanation:
Half the chord is \(8\div2=4\text{ cm}\). The distance \(d\) is
\[
d=\sqrt{5^2-4^2}=\sqrt{25-16}=\sqrt{9}=3\text{ cm}.
\]
So the distance is \(3\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use half the chord and the radius to form a right triangle.

questions.concept: Radius from Chord Length and Distance
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the radius given the chord length and the distance from the center.
questions.question: A chord of length \(24\text{ cm}\) is \(5\text{ cm}\) from the center of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation:
Half the chord is \(24\div2=12\text{ cm}\). The radius \(r\) is
\[
r=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{144+25}=\sqrt{169}=13\text{ cm}.
\]
So the radius is \(13\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use half the chord and the distance from the center as the legs of a right triangle.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the distances from the center for two chords of different lengths in the same circle.
questions.question: In a circle, chord \(AB=24\text{ cm}\) and chord \(CD=10\text{ cm}\). Which chord is closer to the center?
questions.explanation: In the same circle, a longer chord is closer to the center. Since \(24>10\), chord \(AB\) is longer and therefore closer to the center than chord \(CD\).
questions.hint: Recall the relationship between chord length and distance from the center in the same circle.
